profile.description: GCP c4a-highcpu-32 / Axion Neoverse-V2, Nemotron 3.5 streaming 0.6B, int8, cache-aware streaming over WebSocket. One wide worker on a 24-cpu slice, the remaining 8 cpus reserved for whatever generates the load. Screened, not qualified: a ladder found the ceiling, no soak has held it yet.

hardware.smt_policy: OFF; one thread per physical core
hardware.notes: bf16/sve/sve2 are present and the binary issues none of them. That is three unspent levers, not a defect, and --dispatch-map prints them as IDLE so the gap stays visible.

build.notes: No OpenBLAS on this host, so gemm.f32 resolves to our own sgemm. That is what a clean clone gets here.

notes: prefork_workers is 1 ON PURPOSE and it is the measured answer, not the lazy one. The 2026-09-20 W x T sweep, re-scored once lost streams counted as failures, reads: 1x24 holds c=16 with zero losses at every rung; 4x6 and 8x3 hold c=8; 2x12 holds nothing. The narrow topologies looked better only while dropped streams were scored MARGINAL.

http_threads is NOT the compute width. It is the server's HTTP thread pool and a WebSocket stream holds one for its whole life, so it is the concurrency ceiling; the compute pool sizes itself from the process's affinity mask, which is what server_cpus sets.

batch_window_ms is 0 because widening the ready set did not move the ceiling: 40 ms took the mean ready set from 3.69 to 5.85 at c=16 and the ceiling stayed at 16, and 80 ms took it to 7.98 and cost a rung. Kept at 0 until something makes the fixed cost matter again.

MYNAH_ASR_THREADS.why: must be ABSENT: the pool sizes itself from sched_getaffinity, which is what makes server_cpus mean anything. Setting it silently overrides the slice.

MYNAH_ASR_CAPS.why: must be ABSENT: the runtime probe must choose the kernel, and dispatch_required is what checks it chose right.

OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS.why: must be ABSENT: no OpenBLAS is linked here, and a variable that does nothing is a variable someone will later believe did something.

MYNAH_ASR_POOL_SPIN_US.why: must be ABSENT: the default spin has never been swept on this box. The sibling engine found a 16x longer spin budget on aarch64 worth measurable p95; that sweep is owed here and this line is the record that it has not been done.

MYNAH_ASR_STACK_SOLO.why: default, stated here because it is load-bearing: a ready set of one goes through the stacked encoder path. Measured on this box, one binary, flag as the only difference, arms alternated, c=8 on a fresh server each time -- ON 105/104/103 ms emission lag p95, OFF 175/175 ms. The step itself goes 86.7 -> 16.8 ms for a lone stream.

gates.notes: ttfp is deliberately null. The committed English clips start speaking at 0.18 s, 0.64 s and 0.02 s and samples/en/fleurs_long.wav does not start until 23.2 s, so TTFP measured from stream open is measuring leading silence: it was flat at 1660-1760 ms across a ladder whose emission lag tripled. A TTFP gate needs a corpus trimmed to speech onset first.

cost_model_on_the_serving_path.note: Fitted from mynah_asr_step_b_wall_ms_sum / mynah_asr_step_b_count, i.e. the step AS THE SCHEDULER CALLS IT. The bench in isolation says b = 4.58; the serving path is roughly twice that and gets worse with load. B_max = (0.8*320 - 39.5)/8.57 = 25, against a ceiling of 16-20 observed -- the first time the prediction and the measurement have been in the same neighbourhood.

solo_group_ab.note: The third OFF rung is the open stall, not a property of the arm. It landing in the CONTROL arm is what rules the change out as its cause -- a ladder run just before this A/B had shown the failure twice with the change ON, which on its own would have been read as a regression.

provenance.harness: tools/bench/stream_load.py --mode wave --repeat 2, generator pinned to cpus 24-31, one process per stream
notes: The capacity stated is for the 24-cpu SLICE, not for the 32-cpu box, and it is not scaled up. The load generator is one process per stream and shares the machine; the 8 reserved cpus are what keeps it out of the measurement.
status stays `screened` until a soak of at least 10 minutes holds c=16 with transcripts checked. A WAVE may disqualify a rung; it never promotes one.

OPEN DEFECT, not reproduced: a stall in which every stream receives a first partial and then nothing for tens of seconds, seen once at c=8 and once at c=16 on used servers and never on 5 clean repeats. It correlates with prefork -- every prefork topology in the sweep lost streams to it and 1x24 lost none.
